title: Kitty Hawk, 1903
subtitle: Four flights on the North Carolina dunes prove controlled, powered aviation is possible.

models.name: Witness John T Daniels
models.notes: 1903 Kill Devil Hills Lifesaving Service witness John T. Daniels in heavy winter peacoat, wool scarf, wide-brimmed felt hat, and tall boots, squeezing the pneumatic shutter bulb to capture the first flight.

models.name: Launch Rail
models.notes: 60-foot (18.3m) wooden monorail launch track ('Jumbo') made of four 15-foot 2x4 spruce sections laid end-to-end on cross-ties, joined with bolted iron splice plates and topped with an iron running strip.

models.name: Kill Devil Hills Shed
models.notes: 1903 Wright Brothers Kill Devil Hills wooden hangar and camp shed. Board-and-batten rough pine siding, tarpaper gable roof, stove pipe, and large braced hangar doors posed ajar revealing the dark interior.

models.name: Gundlach Korona Camera
models.notes: 1903 Gundlach Korona 5x7 glass-plate field camera on a tall split-rail ash and mahogany wooden tripod with brass hardware, pleated red-mahogany bellows, brass lens assembly, and pneumatic rubber shutter bulb.

scenes.caption: December 17, 1903: the Wrights ready their Flyer on the Carolina dunes.
They invented three-axis control: wing warping, an elevator and a rudder.
At 10:35 Wilbur steadies the wing as Daniels snaps the shutter.
Orville flies 120 feet in 12 seconds: the first powered, controlled flight.
By noon Wilbur flies 852 feet in 59 seconds and proves controlled flight.
